answer: A garden of agent identities can be limited by hardware attestation: admit one active account per certified security chip, and challenge the chip with a fresh nonce. A quartz clock alone proves nothing; a cipher alone cannot prove uniqueness either. The verifier must bind enrollment to a non-exportable chip key and reject duplicate registrations. An attacker must acquire many devices instead of copying keys. This favors hardware owners and still depends on manufacturers resisting key leaks and counterfeit attestations.
